label: Selected cone well-foundedness from acyclicity and anchored regress denial
description: Keep the same actual recipient, world and actual concrete Profile.grounds graph. Acyclicity makes a descending chain injective, so denying an injective chain gives accessibility at the recipient. Accessibility propagates to its finite actual concrete ancestors, which gives well-foundedness on the complete selected cone. The converse excludes an anchored regress without assuming acyclicity of the full actual concrete graph. The two-cycle control has a repeating descending chain and fails cone well-foundedness while satisfying injective regress denial. Composition with the existing SelectedAncestry.necessaryRootAncestor theorem retains the recipient's actual-concrete witness, cone-local contingent grounding and excluded middle. The result supplies one conditional support option for cone well-foundedness, without assuming location coverage or establishing the higher premises.
